 JUDGMENT:

The Petitioners in MVC No.2433/2024 and MVC No.2434/2024 have filed both Petitions against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2433 &
2434/2024 seeking Compensation of 20,00,000/- and Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.
2. Since both these Petitions arises out of the same accident and in view of the Order dated 27.09.2024, these two cases were clubbed together and taken for common disposal.

3. The substance of averments made in both the Petitions are as under:
That on 05.03.2024 at about 4.30 p.m. when the Petitioner in MVC No.2434/2024 was riding his Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-02-KV-5674 along with pillion rider who is the Petitioner in MVC No.2433/2024 by name Vignesh and when they reached near Pramod Layout, Nice road junction, Nice Road, Bengaluru, at that time, one Canter lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-14-5288 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and with high speed and dashed against the petitioners Scooter. Due to the said impact, both Petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

4. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner in MVC SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 No.2433/2024 had taken to Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain hospital, Bengaluru and after first aid treatment, he was shifted to Ganga Medical Centre Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein, the Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient.
The Petitioner had spent Rs.6,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner in MVC No.2434/2024 had taken to Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain hospital, Bengaluru, wherein, the Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient.

The Vignesh R vs Sandeep Kumar on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26572182/
2 Petitioner had spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.

5. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner in MVC No.2433/2024 was hale and healthy and he was working as a Coolie and was earning Rs.22,000/- per month.
6.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner in MVC No.2434/2024 was hale and healthy and he was working as a Coolie and was earning Rs.22,000/- per month.
The accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Canter SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-14-5288 by its driver.
The Respondent No.1 is the Owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the Canter lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-14-5288.
Therefore, both the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners in both petitions.
7. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its detailed Objection Statement.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the accident caused by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioners in both the petitions and the expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioners.
Further it contended that the rider of the motorcycle and the driver of the offending vehicle does not hold valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

On these SCCH 15 6 MVC No.2433 &
2434/2024 grounds, it has prayed to dismiss both the petitions against it.
8. On the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed following Issues.

ISSUES IN MVC No.2433/2024 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 05.03.2024 at about 4.30 p.m., near Pramod layout, Nice road Junction, Nice Road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Canter lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-14-5288?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3. What Order or Award ?

ISSUES IN MVC No.2434/2024 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 05.03.2024 at about 4.30 p.m., near Pramod layout, Nice road Junction, Nice Road, Bengaluru, due to SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Canter lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-14-5288?

3
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?

3 . What Order or Award ?
9.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner in MVC No.2433/2024 got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 12 documents at Ex.P-1 & 2 and Ex.P7 to 16.
The Petitioner in MVC No.2434/2024 got examined himself as P.W.2 and got marked 5 documents at Ex.P-3 to 6 and 17.
Further, the Petitioners have examined three witnesses as PW.3 to 5 and got marked 12 documents at Ex.P18 to 29 and closed their side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence.

10. Having heard the arguments by the learned Counsels for both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the SCCH 15 8 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 Issues in MVC No.2433/2024 are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order,
11.

My answer to the Issues in MVC No.2434/2024 are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :

12. Issue No.1 in MVC No. 2433/2024 and 2434/2024 :- It is the case of the Petitioners that they sustained injuries in the Road Traffic accident which caused by the driver of the offending Canter lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-14- 5288.
13.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 had denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 driver of the offending vehicle.
14. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioners in both the petitions have been examined as P.W.1 and PW.2 and they also examined three witnesses as P.W.3 to 5.
They got marked in total 29 documents at Ex.P1 to 29.

Ex.P7 to 16 are the True copies of FIR,
Complaint, Spot mahazar with Sketch, Statement, Police Notice and Reply, Wound Certificates, IMV Vignesh R vs Sandeep Kumar on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26572182/
4 report and Charge sheet.

15. Upon going through Ex.P7 and 8 i.e., FIR and Complaint shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Hariharan R S/o Rajendran, before Byatrayanapura Traffic Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of the Canter lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-14-5288 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Ex.P9 is the Spot mahazar with Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
SCCH 15 10 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 Ex.P10 is the Statement of the Petitioner.
Ex.P11 and 12 are the Police Notice and Reply.
Ex.P.13 & 14 are the Wound Certificates of the Petitioner in MVC No.2433/2024 which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P15 is the IMV Report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.

Ex.P-16 is the True copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation,
the PSI of Byatrayanapura Traffic Police Station has submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
Ex.P-1 is the Medical bills.
Ex.P2 is the Aadhaar card of the Petitioner in MVC No.2433/2024.
Ex.P-3 is the Discharge summary of the Petitioner in MVC No.2434/2024 which shows that he was admitted as an inpatient.
Ex.P4 is the Medical bills.

Ex.P5 and 6 are the Aadhaar card and DL of the Petitioner in MVC No.2434/2024 and Ex.P.17 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner in MVC No.2434/2024 which shows that the Petitioner had sustained simple injuries.

Further, the Petitioner in MVC No.2433/2024 has examined Dr. Ramesh B as PW.3 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P18 & 19 i.e., OPD book and X-ray and also examined Medical Record Technicians by name S. Nandhakumar and Usha G as PW-4 and 5 and got marked 10 documents at Ex.P20 to 29 i.e., Authorisation Letter, Case sheets, Police intimation and MLC Register extracts.
17. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 and PW.2 in lengthy.
In the cross-examination both PW.1 and PW.2 have denied the suggestions and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the Petitioners.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any oral or documentary evidence to substantiate its Objection Statement contentions.
Hence, the Respondent No.2 has failed to substantiate its Objection Statement contentions.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 driver of the offending vehicle and Petitioners in both the cases had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in both the cases in the "Affirmative".

18. Issue No.2 in MVC No.2433/2024:- As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Canter lorry by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

Vignesh R vs Sandeep Kumar on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26572182/
5 19.
In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 23 years.

Further, in the Aadhaar Card i.e.,
Ex.P-2, the date of birth of the Petitioner was shown as 09.06.2000.
The accident took place on 05.03.2024.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the Petitioner was 23 years, 8 months and 26 days.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident was 24 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.

20. Further, the Petitioner has averred that he was working as a Coolie and was earning Rs.22,000/-
per month.
SCCH 15 13 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 But, he has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.16,500/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
21. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
22.
It is stated in the petition that, in the accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P-13 & 14 issued by the Medical Officer of the Ganga Hospital and Bhagavan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Crush injury present over medial aspect of left ankle joint SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 measuring 14cm X 10cm X 2cm, exposing the underlying lacerated muscles and fractured bone fragments.
Margins of the wound are irregular.
2) 2X1cm abrasion over the medial aspect of left footpath 3) 5X5 cm abrasion over the anterior aspect below left knee
As per the opinion of the doctor, injuries are grievous and simple in nature.

23. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of 40,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
24. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of 25,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
Vignesh R vs Sandeep Kumar on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26572182/
6 25.
The petitioner deposed in his evidence that he has taken the inpatient treatment at Ganga hospital, Bengaluru.
Upon going through Ex.P.21 i.e., Case sheet, which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 06.03.2024 to 18.03.2024.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 13 days.
26. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.33,000/- under this head (@ Rs.16,500/- per month ).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
27.

Admittedly, the petitioner has sustained injuries and SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- (@ Rs.100/- per day for 30 days)
towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/-
towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
28. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent more than 6,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other than towards conveyances.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced medical bills at Ex.P1.
I have gone through the same.
The acceptable medical bills comes to Rs.58,140/-.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at Rs.58,150/-.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for SCCH 15 17 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 Rs.58,150/- under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
29. The Petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.
30. Further, the Petitioner got examined witness by name Dr. Ramesh B as P.W.3 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident.
Further, he assessed the disability of the Petitioner towards Left Lower Limb at 30% and to the whole body at 15%.
Further, PW.3 got marked OPD book and X-ray at Ex.P18 & 19.
In the cross- examination, PW.3 admitted that he has not treated the Petitioner and the fracture of the Petitioner is united.
He denied the other suggestions.

Hence, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the depositions and SCCH 15 18 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 documents exhibited, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 5% would be just and proper.
Vignesh R vs Sandeep Kumar on 9 April, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26572182/
7 31.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 18.

With multiplier of 18, income of Rs.16,500/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 5%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.1,78200/- (Rs.16,500/- x 12 =
1,98,000/-, Rs.1,98,000/-x 18 x 5/100 = 1,78,200/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 1,78,200/- under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
32.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 40,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/-
 SCCH 15 19 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 3.

Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/-
 diet, and conveyance 4. Loss of income during the Rs. 33,000/-
 laid up period

5. Medical expenses Rs. 58,150/-
6. Loss of Future income Rs. 1,78,200/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,52,350/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

33. Issue No.2 in MVC No.2434/2024:- As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Canter lorry by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
34. It is stated in the petition that, the Petitioner is aged 24 years at the time of accident.
The Petitioner has produced his Aadhaar card and DL at Ex.P5 and 6, which shows his date of birth was 20.10.1999.
The accident has taken place on SCCH 15 20 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 05.03.2024.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the Petitioner was 24 years, 4 months, 15 days.
Hence, at the time of accident, the Petitioner was aged about 25 years.
35. It is established that the Petitioner had suffered injury in the Road Traffic Accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending Container lorry.
The Petitioner has contended that he had sustained grievous injuries and he spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- for his medical treatment and other incidental charges.

The Petitioner has produced Wound Certificate at Ex.P17 issued at Bhagawan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein it shows that the Petitioner Vignesh R vs Sandeep Kumar on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26572182/
8

sentences.text: had sustained Abrasion over outer aspect of the left eye, abrasion over philtrum of nose, abrasion over left shoulder joint and tenderness present over the cervical spine.
The Doctor has opined that all injuries are simple in nature.
36. The Petitioner did not choose to examine the doctor who issued the Wound Certificate as per Ex.P17.
The Petitioner SCCH 15 21 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 has produced the Medical bills to prove expenditure towards medicines.
Apart from this, the Petitioner has not produced any documents to show that, he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment as contended in the petition.
Ex.P3 is the Discharge summary which shows that he was admitted from 05.03.2024 to 06.03.2024 as an inpatient.
37. Though the Petitioner has averred that he has become unable to do his work because of the injuries sustained by him, no Physical Disability Certificate has been produced.
Considering the gravity of the injuries, pain and suffering, Medical expenses, food and nourishment and conveyance it would be lawful to award global compensation of Rs.60,000/- to the Petitioner.

38. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Canter lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-14-5288.
In this case, the SCCH 15 22 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative" in both cases.

39. Issue No.3 in both cases: From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner in MVC No.2433/2024 is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,52,350/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
40. The Petitioner in MVC No.2434/2024 is entitled for global compensation of Rs.60,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
 SCCH 15 23 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024  ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner in MVC No.2433/2024 against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

9
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner in MVC No.2434/2024 against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner in M.V.C. No. 2433/2024 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,52,350/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.

The Petitioner in M.V.C. No. 2434/2024 is entitled for global compensation of Rs.60,000/- along with cost and simple SCCH 15 24 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 in both the cases are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle in both cases, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner in MVC No.2433/2024, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E-payment after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years.

SCCH 15 25 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 On deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, since the amount is meager, the entire amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner in MVC No.2434/2024 by way of E-payment after his proper identification.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
respectively in both cases.
Draw Award accordingly.

Keep the Original Judgment in M.V. C. No.2433/2024 and the copy of the Judgment in M.V.C.
No.2434/2024.

The Petitioners in MVC No.2433/2024 and MVC No.2434/2024 have filed both Petitions against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2433 &
2434/2024 seeking Compensation of 20,00,000/- and Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.33,000/- under this head (@ Rs.16,500/- per month ).

The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner in MVC No.2433/2024 against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner in M.V.C. No. 2433/2024 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,52,350/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Petitioner in M.V.C. No. 2434/2024 is entitled for global compensation of Rs.60,000/- along with cost and simple SCCH 15 24 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 in both the cases are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle in both cases, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner in MVC No.2433/2024, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E-payment after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years.
SCCH 15 25 MVC No.2433 & 2434/2024 On deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, since the amount is meager, the entire amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner in MVC No.2434/2024 by way of E-payment after his proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
respectively in both cases.
Draw Award accordingly.
